 As part of the Product Security Engineering team, you’ll focus on reducing risk at scale by building the security infrastructure, automation, and tooling that empowers engineers to ship secure products with confidence. We work closely with engineering and product teams throughout the software development lifecycle (SDLC), embedding secure-by-default practices and delivering scalable solutions. 
 Product Security Engineers create impact by implementing security tooling, writing custom security rules, and building frameworks that address broad classes of vulnerabilities. In addition to proactive development, we support teams through threat modeling, documentation, and education to uplift security culture across Dropbox. 
 
  Our Engineering Career Framework is    viewable by anyone outside the company    and describes what’s expected for our engineers at each of our career levels. Check out our blog post on this topic and more    here   .

 Build and maintain security tools, automation, and libraries to enable secure-by-default development across engineering teams. 
 Design and implement custom security rules  (e.g.,  Semgrep, CodeQL) to detect and prevent common and emerging vulnerability patterns. 
 Act as a subject matter expert on application security across web, mobile, and desktop environments. 
 Improve and scale the Secure Development Lifecycle  (SDLC)  by integrating tools, checks, and processes into engineering workflows. 
 Perform targeted code reviews, and develop follow-up tooling or controls to prevent regressions. 
 Collaborate cross-functionally with engineering, product, GRC, and AI/ML teams to proactively address security risks, especially in fast-moving and emerging tech areas.

 Demonstrated ability to work across the SDLC, including supporting and interpreting findings from penetration tests and bug bounty reports. 
 Familiarity with modern tech stacks, including microservices, CI/CD pipelines, and cloud-native environments. 
 Solid understanding of common vulnerability classes  (e.g.,  injection, XSS, authN/authZ issues) and practical mitigation strategies.

jobs.description:
Headquarters:  Canada - Remote
 

 Elation Health is deeply committed to helping independent primary care practices take better care of their patients. Since 2010, we've built a clinical-first, collaborative EHR platform — and with the addition of Elation Billing, we're bringing that same clinical-first philosophy to the revenue side of the practice, so billing works  with  the chart instead of around it. 
 Elation Health is searching for a  Support Subject Matter Expert in Elation Billing  — someone who has already done real medical billing and revenue cycle management work, not someone learning it on the job. This is a hands-on, case-based role embedded directly in our support queue: you'll bring practitioner-level RCM judgment to the billing cases our Technical Support Specialists can't fully resolve through process or AI-assisted troubleshooting alone, and you'll help the rest of the team get sharper at spotting those cases in the first place. 
 This isn't a back-office consulting role. You'll be working live cases day to day alongside our support team, diagnosing whether an issue is a product bug, a payer-specific quirk, or a mismatch between how a practice actually operates and how they've configured their billing workflow — then resolving it with the kind of judgment that only comes from having sat inside a claims lifecycle before. 
 Responsibilities 
 
 Serve as the Elation Billing product line's embedded RCM expert, owning complex billing and revenue cycle cases that require practitioner-level judgment — claims lifecycle issues, CPT/ICD-10 coding logic, payer adjudication and denial patterns, A/R and collections workflows. 
 Act as the go-to resource for case swarms and escalations within Elation Billing whenever a Technical Support Specialist's investigation surfaces a billing nuance beyond scripted troubleshooting. 
 Diagnose a practice's underlying billing context — payment model (insurance-taking vs. DPC), staffing structure, and prior workflow choices — to distinguish genuine product issues from configuration or workflow mismatches, rather than treating every case as a symptom in isolation. 
 Partner with Product and Prod Dev, turning recurring billing edge cases, payer-specific patterns, and denial trends into structured feedback that can inform the roadmap. 
 Contribute to and maintain the team's billing-related knowledge base, SOPs, and macros, and help calibrate the AI Case Assistant's billing-related suggestions so resolutions compound across the team rather than living only in your own case history. 
 Help build the broader team's baseline RCM literacy — sharing real-world billing context so Specialists can better anticipate the issues different practice types are prone to. 
 Track and report on billing-case quality and resolution metrics within your scope, and flag systemic patterns rather than resolving the same root cause case-by-case indefinitely. 
 
 Requirements 
 
 3+ years of hands-on medical billing / revenue cycle management experience — claims submission, payer follow-up, denial management, and A/R — brought in from outside a support organization, not built up through support tenure. 
 Working fluency in CPT/ICD-10 coding logic, claims adjudication, and payer-specific billing rules across commercial and government payers. 
 Experience working within an EHR, practice management, or medical billing platform (e.g., Epic, athenahealth, Waystar, or similar). 
 Strong written and verbal communicator, able to translate complex billing and RCM concepts into clear guidance for both practices and internal teams. 
 Comfortable working directly in a live case queue - this is a frontline, hands-on role, not a periodic-consulting one. 
 Self-directed and detail-oriented, with the judgment to know when a case needs to go beyond a scripted answer. 
 
 Preferred 
 
 Certification such as CPB (Certified Professional Biller), CRCR (Certified Revenue Cycle Representative), or CHFP (in progress or completed). 
 Prior experience supporting independent primary care or small-group practices specifically. 
 Experience on a support, customer success, or implementation team at a SaaS/EHR company. 
 Exposure to AI-assisted support or case-management tooling. 
 Six Sigma, Lean, or other process-improvement background.

jobs.title: CircleCI: Staff Software Engineer
jobs.description:
Headquarters:  Canada (Remote), United States (Remote), United Kingdom (Remote) Mexico City, Mexico - Hybrid
 

 About CircleCI Engineering 
 CI/CD has been solved. Now it's being reinvented. AI agents don't just run pipelines. They write code, trigger builds, interpret failures, and propose fixes. The interfaces that developers use to understand and trust that work don't exist yet. We're building them. 
 At CircleCI, our guiding principles aren't posters on a wall. We learn fast: we run experiments, accept failure, and scale what works. We think like the customer: every decision connects back to the developer sitting in front of a failing build at 2 am. We own the outcome: not just our slice of it, but the whole thing. If that's how you already work, you'll fit here. 
 Team-Agnostic Placement 
 We don't hire for a team. We hire for CircleCI. Where you land depends on where your strengths create the most leverage, and we figure that out together. You might own the CI pipeline experience, deploy and release tooling, notification infrastructure, monetization flows, AI agent surfaces, or the foundational web platform. The through line across all of it is the same: full-stack ownership, a high bar for craft, and work that directly shapes how tens of thousands of developers experience CircleCI every day. 
 What You'll Do 
 
  Build AI-natively.  AI is how we work. It's not a productivity layer on top of engineering, but the default starting point for how problems get approached and solved. 
  Own technical strategy for your domain.  You decide when and how the architecture evolves, balancing technical debt against velocity. When a project spans teams, you're the one who breaks down the ambiguity and takes ownership of whether it lands. 
  Invent new interfaces.  Software delivery is being reinvented. Pipelines run autonomously, generate fixes, and surface results that need human judgment. The tools developers use to understand, trust, and act on that work don't exist yet. You'll define what they look like and establish the patterns the team builds on. 
  Own the full stack,   at scale.  Build features end-to-end in Go, React, and TypeScript. Your ownership extends past your own code to the systems and teams around it. 
  Connect engineering to the business.  Partner directly with Product and Engineering Management to translate business goals into technical strategy. You understand the "why" behind the roadmap and use it to make tradeoffs. 
  Champion observability.  Drive monitoring and alerting strategy across your domain, not just your own services. Use Honeycomb, Datadog, and Rollbar to reduce noise and improve the org's ability to diagnose problems quickly. 
  Mentor at scale.  Mentor multiple engineers at once. Build the systems and documentation that transfer knowledge and remove single points of failure, not just your own. 
 
 What You'll Bring 
 
  AI-native engineering practices.  You use AI tools daily and can speak to what you've built, where they changed your approach, and where they fall short. 
  A track record of shipping at scale.  You've built and owned systems that other engineers build on. 8+ years of production full-stack experience, with a history of taking accountability for outcomes. 
  Full-stack depth.  Strong across the stack — React and TypeScript on the frontend, Go on the backend, owning API design, data modeling, and service integration. 
  System design  , across domains.  You own architecture decisions that span multiple systems and teams. You make the tradeoff calls, document the reasoning, and are the person others escalate to when the answer isn't obvious. 
  Business acumen.  You understand how your domain connects to the broader business, and you use that context to guide technical decisions, not just implement them. 
  Technical leadership.  You mentor engineers, give direct feedback on technical direction, and raise the quality bar across teams through how you engage in reviews and design discussions, not just what you ship. 
 
 Sound like you? 
 You've stopped waiting for AI to mature and are already building with it, not as a productivity trick, but as a core part of how you think about problems. You care about the product as much as the code. You're drawn to work where the patterns don't exist yet and the best answer requires you to invent it. If that's how you already operate, we want to talk. 
 
  The salary range listed reflects the wide geographic scope of this posting, as we hire across the United States and Canada. Actual compensation is determined based on a combination of factors, including but not limited to skills, experience, job-related knowledge, and geographic location. As a result, the starting salary offered may vary and could fall anywhere within the posted range, and not all candidates should expect to receive an offer at the top of the range.     Canada Base Pay Range   $195,000  —  $265,000 CAD     United Kingdom Base Pay Range   £125,000  —  £170,000

jobs.title: CircleCI: Staff Software Engineer, Delivery Engineering
jobs.description:
Headquarters:  Remote, Canada (EST) OR Remote, US (EST) OR Remote, UK
 



 About CircleCI Engineering 
 CI/CD has been solved. Now it's being reinvented. AI agents don't just run pipelines. They write code, trigger builds, interpret failures, and propose fixes. The interfaces that developers use to understand and trust that work don't exist yet. We're building them. 
 At CircleCI, our guiding principles aren't posters on a wall. We learn fast: we run experiments, accept failure, and scale what works. We think like the customer: every decision connects back to the developer sitting in front of a failing build at 2 am. We own the outcome: not just our slice of it, but the whole thing. If that's how you already work, you'll fit here. 


 About Delivery Engineering 
 Delivery Engineering enables CircleCI engineers to deliver quickly, confidently, and securely. We provide the tools and resources that make standard patterns and best practices simple to adopt, and we reduce toil. 
 Our current focus is the agentic software development lifecycle: how changes are found, planned, built, reviewed, merged, and measured as AI agents take on more of the work. We evaluate the harnesses, repository patterns, skills, and agentic tooling available, decide what our teams should standardize on, and build and support the shared tooling other teams depend on. 
 We're a small, very senior team, and everyone on it shapes where we go. Every improvement we make compounds across the organization. 


 What You'll Do 
 
  Build AI-natively.  AI is how we work. It's not a productivity layer on top of engineering, but the default starting point for how problems get approached and solved. 
  Shape how CircleCI builds software with agents.  Help define the end-to-end agentic SDLC, from identifying a change through planning, execution, pull request, merge, and measuring impact afterward. Evaluate shared tooling and patterns, and help decide what teams standardize on. 
  Start from how our teams actually work.  Spend time with engineering teams to understand their workflows and where they get stuck. Use what you learn to drive decisions and direction that teams adopt because the work fits how they operate. 
  Build platforms, not one-offs.  Build and support shared tooling that other teams depend on, and own its adoption as much as its delivery. A tool nobody uses isn't done. 
  Measure what matters.  Instrument agent usage and outcomes so we know what improves throughput and quality and what just burns tokens. Treat cost, model choice, and reliability as design concerns. 
  Make build-vs-buy calls.  Evaluate models, vendors, and open-source tools against our needs, and choose the path that gets engineers the most leverage. 
  Lead through influence.  Write the design docs, lead technical discussions across teams, and mentor engineers across the org as they adopt agentic workflows. 
 


 What You'll Bring 
 
  Direct experience driving agentic developer experience efforts.  You've driven an initiative that changed how an engineering organization builds software with AI agents. You can speak to what you built, how you measured its impact, how you drove adoption, and what didn't work. 
  Hands-on depth with agentic tooling.  You work daily with coding agents, agent harnesses, MCP, and skills or prompt design. You know how to evaluate agent output and reason about model and token economics. 
  A platform mindset.  You've built and supported internal platforms or developer tooling that other engineers build on and rely on, and driven their adoption. 
  Backend depth in Go.  You've owned production backend services in Go, including API design, data modeling, and service integration. 
  A track record at staff scope.  8+ years of production engineering experience, including technical decisions that spanned multiple teams and accountability for whether they landed. 
  Decision-making grounded in your users.  You build direction by listening first. You turn the needs of many teams into clear tradeoffs, document your reasoning, and bring people along. 
 
 This role is open to candidates based in Europe or in the Eastern time zone. 


 Sound like you? 
 You've stopped waiting for AI to mature and are already building with it, not as a productivity trick, but as a core part of how you think about problems. You care about the engineers using your tools as much as the code behind them. You're drawn to work where the patterns don't exist yet and the best answer requires you to invent it with the people who'll use it. If that's how you already operate, we want to talk.

Engineers here are trusted to make decisions, shape technical direction, and move quickly while collaborating closely with Product and Design. 
  What You'll Do  
 
 Use your deep expertise in full-stack development (TypeScript, JavaScript, Go, and React) to ship reliable, scalable, performant code across our product suite, and set the patterns that others on the team and across the org follow.  
 Own the technical direction for our product area, including the web app, CLI, MCP, SDK, API, and docs, by defining architecture and roadmap alongside your manager, Product, and Design, and make tradeoffs explicit so decisions are easy to understand and revisit 
 Lead large, ambiguous projects that span multiple teams from conception to delivery, such as our application rewrite and upcoming CLI rework, writing RFCs, driving alignment, and managing risk and timelines

 Mentor and grow engineers through code reviews, design reviews, pairing, and sponsorship, raising the technical level of the whole team 
 Practice proactive async communication and create visibility across projects by documenting your workflows and decision-making clearly 
 Participate in on-call rotations, lead incident follow-up, and drive continuous improvement efforts that reduce technical debt and prevent recurring problems 
 Collaborate with cross-functional teams and engineering leadership to shape user flows that enhance the developer experience across our platform, and contribute to hiring and team growth

 Deep expertise in TypeScript and JavaScript, with a long track record of designing, shipping, and maintaining production-quality software in modern full-stack environments

  Are interested in new, innovative models of care that balance evidence-based approaches with creative ideas.

  Google Suite (gmail, sheets, docs, etc)   
  Slack

  Competitive health, vision and dental plans

Headquarters:  United States
      URL:   https://www.antora.com 
 

  Antora Energy delivers affordable, reliable energy to industry, data centers, and the grid. Our thermal batteries turn low-cost electricity into always-on heat and power, without supply-constrained critical minerals or multi-year construction timelines. 
 We are growing our company with people who put team and mission first, value connection through laughter and joy, and work with humility and openness. We are committed to building a diverse, passionate, and creative team dedicated to a future powered by abundant, clean, low-cost energy.     
   
  Position Summary  
   
 The Senior Power Procurement Manager will lead utility tariff and power purchase negotiations from first engagement through execution, owning a portfolio of medium- to high-complexity deals across one or more ISOs/RTOs. This is a hands-on individual contributor role with no direct reports: the person will draft and negotiate term sheets and definitive agreements, build and pressure-test deal models, coordinate cross-functional inputs, and serve as the day-to-day point of contact with utility counterparts. They will lead complex, multi-site negotiations, pilot new commercial constructs, and are expected to become Antora's recognized expert for a region. 
   
   
  Roles & Responsibilities  
   
 
 
  Deal Execution & Negotiation  
 
 Lead day-to-day negotiations and the overall close plan for utility tariffs, energy service agreements, and PPAs. 
 Draft and negotiate term sheets; lead definitive agreement negotiations alongside counsel; negotiate standard tariff rate changes per playbook. 
 Support capacity and power sales origination, including preparing and negotiating MOUs, term sheets, and off-take agreements with utilities, hyperscalers, and other large-load customers. 
 Help shape deal structures that fit Antora's unique load profile. 
 Coordinate Finance, Legal, Policy, Business Development, and Engineering inputs; run cross-functional working sessions to align positions, timelines, and technical constraints. 
 
 
 Own financial model architecture for deals: select modeling approaches, set key assumptions, run sensitivities and stress tests, validate inputs, and QA models built by others. 
 
 
  Utility & Counterparty Relationships  
 
 Serve as the primary point of contact with utility managers and directors. 
 Build deep regional knowledge of priority ISOs/RTOs, utilities, and tariff landscapes, growing into a go-to resource for at least one region. 
 Partner with Business Development to qualify and advance opportunities, ensuring smooth handoffs from early engagement to active negotiation. 
 
 
  Regulatory Support & Team Contribution  
 
 Support regulatory work by drafting comments, exhibits, and data responses; may represent Antora in staff workshops and by testifying in regulatory forums. 
 Surface patterns across deals (common counterparty objections, emerging tariff structures, regulatory shifts) and propose playbook language updates for senior review. 
 Informally mentor junior team members on models, redlines, and negotiation prep. 
 
 
 
   
  Key Qualifications  
   
 
 6–12+ years of experience in power procurement, energy origination, utility negotiations, or energy commercial roles. 
 Demonstrated deal track record of leading successful Power Procurement Agreement or Electric Service Agreement   negotiations. 
 Solid working knowledge of utility tariff design, wholesale power markets, and the commercial mechanics of how large loads contract for energy and grid services, with depth in at least one region or ISO. 
 Hands-on experience drafting and negotiating term sheets and definitive agreements alongside counsel. 
 Strong financial modeling skills, ability to build, stress-test, and QA deal models and translate results into negotiation positions. 
 Sound commercial judgment within guardrails: knowing which terms to hold, which to trade, and when a deviation needs to be escalated.

Nobody checks every box - we’re looking for candidates that are particularly strong in a few areas, and have some interest and capabilities in others.  The Mission  The AI Gateway team is on a mission to build the central nervous system for the agentic era, enabling developers to securely and reliably connect, observe, and manage their AI and ML services at scale. Some of the gateway’s more advanced capabilities, such as intelligent model routing, semantic caching, request classification, and content guardrails, work best when backed by small, purpose-built models.   Own the technical direction for model-backed AI Gateway features, from design to production rollout.  
  Build and maintain high-performance components for  Kong ’s AI Gateway in Rust and Lua.  
  Train, fine-tune, and evaluate models for specific gateway use cases, such as classifiers for intelligent routing, embeddings for semantic caching, and guardrail models.  
  Curate and maintain the datasets used for training and evaluation, and define the metrics and thresholds that decide whether a model is good enough to ship.  
  Integrate models into the gateway request path, optimizing inference for latency, throughput, and memory footprint.  
  Troubleshoot bugs, tune performance, and do low-level optimizations across both the gateway and the model serving stack.  
  Work with product management and other engineering teams to turn model capabilities into reliable, documented product features.  
  Mentor other engineers on the team on ML practices and model integration.  
  What You’ll Bring  The Toolkit  
  3+ years of experience in server-side software development: building and debugging applications that are highly scalable, distributed, reliable and resilient.  
  2+ years of experience in machine learning: building, training and evaluating models for production or research.  
  Proficiency with tensor-based deep learning frameworks, in Python and beyond.  
  Experience with dataset curation and evaluation methodology.  
  Experience running models in production outside of Python, optimizing inference for latency and memory (e.g. ONNX Runtime, quantization, batching).  
  Working knowledge of embeddings and vector databases.  
  Hands-on expertise with Linux systems.  
  The  Kong  DNA  
  Ownership: You take full ownership of your work from concept to production, including the documentation: engineers at  Kong  write the documentation for their products.  
  Pragmatism: You can tell when a model is the right tool and when a simpler solution is, and you measure before you decide.  
  Collaboration: You communicate clearly in writing and work effectively with a remotely distributed team.  
  Leadership: You make and explain technical trade-offs where there is no established playbook.  
  Bonus Points  
  Contributions to open-source software projects.  
  Proficiency in Rust, Lua or C.  
  Familiarity with the Rust ML ecosystem (e.g. Candle, Burn, tokenizers).  
  Experience with MLOps tooling and pipelines for training, versioning, and deploying models.  
  Experience with experiment tracking tools (e.g. MLflow, Weights & Biases).  
  Experience with LLM post-training techniques such as LoRA or other parameter-efficient fine-tuning methods.  
  Knowledge of networking fundamentals and protocols on both L4 and L7 (TCP/IP, HTTP/2, gRPC).  
  Hands-on experience with NGINX and OpenResty.

jobs.description:
From empowering entrepreneurs to build successful businesses, to supporting their clients to arrange 'me time' moments, we're in the business of elevating people - helping them to thrive and feel fantastic. Lifting others up can be hard, heavy work, and we passionately believe that the sense of purpose and personal satisfaction this brings are worth it.  What started in Poland is now an international, cloud-based marketplace that's scaling rapidly. We bring independent business owners together with their customers on a product that connects creative communities and opens up worlds of opportunities.  For our providers, our products offer services for getting booked, paid, and building a loyal client base. For their clients, we're where they can find their favourite spots, discover new businesses and book appointments in an instant.  Working in a rapidly growing, ever-changing scale-up comes with its own set of opportunities and challenges. If you prefer a stable environment, with clear processes and structures then, we've got to be honest, you won't always find that here. However, if you enjoy inventively solving problems with others, helping create clarity when things get confusing, and prioritising your own path within ambiguity, then the chances are that you'll love the opportunities available to grow your career at  Booksy .   The people you'll like to work with and things you'll enjoy impacting:   As a  Data Platform Engineer  reporting to the Data Platform Engineering Manager in our Data Platform team (part of Data and Strategic Analytics), your purpose will be to help build and run the foundations every data team at  Booksy  works on. Our platform runs on Google Cloud, the other data teams are our customers, and we're open-source-first. You'll:  
 Design and build platform components (deployment, monitoring, access, ingestion) and own them end to end in production, runbooks included 
 Develop Terraform/Terragrunt modules for BigQuery, Cloud Composer, GKE, Cloud Run and networking 
 Build GitLab CI pipelines and reusable tooling, including AI-powered tools and agents that help other engineers 
 Apply governance and security controls (policy tags, DLP, Dataplex, IAM) by default 
 Introduce new tools, move teams onto them and retire what they replace, as the platform evolves toward a lakehouse 
  There's no people management here. A senior engineer and your manager are close by for the bigger calls, and a published seniority matrix shows what the next level looks like.  Requirements   Essentially, to ensure you succeed in this role you're going to need…   
 Experience in data platform, infrastructure, or backend/DevOps engineering, including hands-on Terraform on GCP or another major cloud 
 Solid Python and strong SQL, with version control, code review, tests and CI as your defaults 
 Experience with GitLab CI (or similar), Docker and Kubernetes, plus working knowledge of administering BigQuery or a comparable cloud data warehouse 
 Fluent use of AI-assisted development tools (e.g. Cursor, Claude), with the judgement to decide what to delegate and how to test what comes back 
 At a minimum we require conversational level English language skills, plus clear written English, since you'll document for teams across time zones. Why? English is our company language and is used for any business-wide communications, so we need you to be able to speak English to feel like an integrated part of  Booksy . 
  It will also help you to have…  
 Experience operating Cloud Composer / Airflow 
 Experience with Dataplex or DLP 
 Exposure to PySpark and open table formats (Apache Iceberg / Delta Lake) 
  Benefits  Some benefits we offer are:  
 We're proudly distributed across the globe, with each market being remote-first. 
 Depending on which market you're joining, you might have office access or be fully remote - either works. All we ask is that you're based in the country/region this role is advertised in. 
 Additional benefits that might differ depending on the location. You shall be provided with the benefits details during or after your first conversation with one of our TA Specialists. 
  Our Diversity and Inclusion Commitment:  We work in a highly creative and diverse industry so it goes without saying that we strive to create an inclusive environment for all. We welcome people from all backgrounds and are committed to fair consideration in our hiring process. If you have any accessibility needs or require reasonable adjustments during the interview process, please contact us at , so we can best support you.  Kindly submit your application and CV in English to ensure it is successfully reviewed.  Originally posted on  Himalayas

Our SmartMast™ system transforms commercial and civilian vessels into a persistent, distributed sensing network—combining HD video, AI, radar, RF sensing, and AIS to deliver real-time maritime domain awareness at global scale. With 600+ sensors deployed across 25+ countries and more than 400,000 vessels identified outside of AIS, we are setting a new standard for what ocean surveillance and safety can look like. We are a mission-driven, high-velocity team building dual-use technology for defense agencies, coast guards, and commercial maritime operators.   Job Description:   We are seeking a Manufacturing Engineer to support our team’s growing production demands and process improvement goals across  Quartermaster ’s SmartMast™ systems and related marine products. Based out of our Arlington, VA office, this role will play a critical part in onboarding and transitioning production to additional contract manufacturers (CMs), reducing assembly downtime, improving first-pass yield, and freeing up our core R&D engineers to focus on next-generation design and product improvements.  The right candidate brings strong hands-on experience scaling electromechanical hardware production with external contract manufacturers, translating engineering designs into repeatable manufacturing processes, and driving continuous improvements on the production floor.   Key Responsibilities:   
  Lead manufacturing transfer, line setup, and onboarding activities as  Quartermaster  expands production across new and existing contract manufacturers (CMs).  
  Develop, optimize, and maintain manufacturing work instructions, assembly procedures, test fixtures, and tooling to reduce build times and prevent assembly errors.  
  Drive continuous process improvements across production lines to reduce downtime, eliminate bottlenecks, and increase first-pass yield and throughput.  
  Partner closely with Mechanical, Electrical, and Quality Engineering teams on Design for Manufacturability and Assembly (DFMA), Engineering Change Orders (ECOs), and New Product Introduction (NPI) builds.  
  Troubleshoot production-line equipment, test station, and assembly issues in real time, implementing durable corrective actions so design engineers can stay focused on future product development.  
  Track production metrics (cycle time, yield, scrap/rework rates, line capacity) and collaborate with Supply Chain and CMs to support scaling production volumes.  
   Qualifications (Preferred):   
  Bachelor’s degree in Manufacturing, Mechanical, Industrial, or Electrical Engineering, or equivalent practical experience.  
  3–5+ years of experience in manufacturing engineering for electromechanical hardware, marine electronics, aerospace/defense, or ruggedized outdoor systems.  
  Proven experience working directly with contract manufacturers (CMs) to transfer, qualify, and scale hardware production lines.  
  Strong command of DFMA principles, assembly tooling/fixture design, process validation (PFMEA, Control Plans), and lean manufacturing methodologies.  
  Hands-on experience writing clear work instructions, managing BOMs/ECOs, and troubleshooting electro-mechanical assembly and test workflows.  
  Ability to work independently and communicate clearly across internal engineering teams, supply chain, and external manufacturing partners.  
  CAD proficiency (e.g., Onshape, SolidWorks) for designing assembly jigs, fixtures, and line layouts is a plus.  
   Work Environment:   
  Based at  Quartermaster ’s Arlington, VA office with flexible working hours and occasional intensive sprints aligned to production ramps and CM transitions.  
  Occasional travel (up to ~25%) to contract manufacturers, component suppliers, or integration facilities.  
  Opportunity to work on innovative projects with a global impact.

jobs.title: Legion: Senior Integration Engineer
jobs.description:
Headquarters:  Remote, Mexico
 

  Senior Integration Engineer  
  Remote, Mexico  
  JOB OVERVIEW  
 Are you passionate about building large-scale applications leveraging public cloud services and integration design patterns? As an Integration Engineer, you will work on developing and maintaining Integration & Automation Solutions for Legion WFM customers. 
   
  RESPONSIBILITIES AND DUTIES  
 Integration Engineers provide leadership, facilitate analysis and design tasks, and support multiple Legion teams in developing an enterprise's solution architecture. Job responsibilities are grouped across four key areas: Technical Integrations, Customer-Centric Consulting, Legion Product Expertise, and a Commitment to One Another. 
 Please note this role involves participation in on-call rotation. 
 Technical Integrations 
 
 Design and implement scalable integration architectures connecting Legion with HR, POS, Payroll, and other enterprise systems. 
 Design, Build, and Test integrations using Workato 
 Develop secure and efficient REST APIs within Legion's API-driven ecosystem. 
 Ensure high-performance, reliable integrations using modern cloud platforms. 
 Engage with architects and engineers for design collaboration and code reviews. 
 Improve development practices and stay ahead of agile software engineering trends. 
 
 Legion Product Expertise 
 
 Gain and maintain deep knowledge of Legion's product and integration ecosystem. 
 Identify, report, and prioritize product bugs and enhancements. 
 Work with core engineering and production engineering teams to improve backend reliability and troubleshoot production issues 
 Stay updated on new releases and enhancements to drive product adoption. 
 Write secure, enterprise-grade integration code using leading platforms and technologies. 
 Write well-designed, testable, efficient code 
 Contribute to all phases of the development lifecycle 
 Conduct peer code reviews to ensure code quality and maintainability. 
 
 Team Collaboration & Mentorship 
 
 Share expertise and mentor junior engineers, fostering a culture of knowledge-sharing. 
 Contribute to best practices for integration and internal technical documentation. 
 Support process improvements and advocate for scalable, sustainable integrations. 
 Commit to high-quality work, setting personal and team objectives aligned with organizational goals. 
 Standard shift working hours: 0900-1800 
 This role involves participation in on-call rotation. 
 This role may require work outside of normal business hours. 
 
  REQUIRED SKILLS AND QUALIFICATIONS  
 
 7+ years of business/information/solution/technical architecture experience 
 Graduate of a university with a Bachelor's or Master's degree in a relevant STEM field, including Information Systems, Engineering, Computer Science, or another relevant degree 
 Must be able to work as a team player, yet can work independently. 
 Analytical, results-driven, and have a solution-oriented approach 
 Possess exceptional interpersonal and English communication skills, including verbal, written presentation, and listening. 
 3+ years of experience with event-driven Architecture and Microservices 
 Demonstrated deep technical expertise in Integration technologies and protocols such as HTTP, HTTPS, FTP, SFTP, SOAP, REST, JMS, JDBC 
 Experience using Linux/Unix environments 
 Demonstrate proficiency with Core Java. 
 Experience with Relational Databases, SQL and JDBC (one of Oracle, PostgreSQL, SQL Server, etc.) 
 2+ years of experience using AWS technologies such as AWS CDK, Cloud formation, S3, ECS, EKS, and EC2 
 Demonstrate experience with test-driven development. 
 Strong experience with Java/RESTful web services 
 Exposure to agile software development leveraging toolsets (e.g., Jira, GitHub, Jenkins) 
 Demonstrate knowledge and experience with CI/CD processes and tools. 
 Proven track record of using problem-solving / root-cause analysis 
 
  PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS AND ATTRIBUTES  
 
 The ideal candidate has workforce management integration experience 
 Preferred experience in the design and implementation of scalable integration solutions with integration platforms such as Workato, SAP BTP Integration Suite, Dell Boomi, Jitterbit, SnapLogic  
 Proactive and able to command respect through intelligence, hard work, and persistence 
 Technical consulting experience. 
 Experience of working with Docker and other isolation technologies. 
 Experience working with external applications integrations end-to-end such as Workday, SAP, etc. 
 
  COMPENSATION & BENEFITS  
 At Legion, we offer competitive compensation and benefits packages to all employees. As a fully remote employer, pay for positions is determined using local, national, and industry-specific survey data.
